department: Revenue Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
what_it_is: The Legal Heir Certificate is a certificate from the Revenue Department of Tamil Nadu. You can ask for it online through e-Sevai. The Tahsildar gives it. The High Court says it only shows the Tahsildar's view of how the family is related to the person who died. It does not change anyone's legal rights.
who_can_apply: Any one family member named in the certificate can apply for all. If the person who died was married, that is father, mother, spouse, sons and daughters. If unmarried, that is father, mother, brothers and sisters. If no adult heir is alive, a child can apply through a guardian.
documents: Death certificate of the person who died
Proof of where the person who died lived, such as Aadhaar, voter ID, passport, bank or post office passbook, driving licence or pension order
Proof of how each heir is related, such as marriage certificate, passport, voter ID, Aadhaar, community certificate, driving licence, or birth certificates or TCs of all children
Self-declarations, and other papers the e-Sevai list asks for in special cases (divorce, second marriage, adoption, guardianship)
how_to_apply: Make a free login on the e-Sevai citizen site with 'sign up', or go to an e-Sevai centre. You need a CAN (Citizen Access Number). Fill the form, upload your papers and pay. When the officer approves and signs it digitally, you can download the certificate. Check where it is with 'Check Status' and your application number. Apply to the Tahsildar of the area where the person who died usually lived. If you disagree with the Tahsildar's order, you can appeal to the Revenue Divisional Officer within one year.
where_to_apply: Any e-Sevai centre (Common Service Centre), or online at tnesevai.tn.gov.in.
fee: Rs 60 service charge at e-Sevai. No department charge (Rs 0).
time_limit: A 2022 Government Order sets about one week for each step: the VAO or RI checks your papers in one week, the RI enquires in one week, and the Tahsildar gives the certificate within one week after the RI's report.
validity: The Tahsildar must not write that it is valid only for six months, or set any other time limit.
